step1_analysis.description: A 5-stage ring oscillator with a voltage-to-current converter front-end. The input control voltage (VEA) drives a unity-gain operational amplifier that sets the current into a current mirror, which in turn controls the virtual ground (V_C) of the ring oscillator, thereby tuning its frequency.

paper_reference.title: A Programmable Integrated Digital Controller for Switching Converters With Dual-Band Switching and Complex Pole-Zero Compensation

center_frequency.description: Oscillation frequency at the nominal control voltage (VEA = 0.9V).

sky130_expected.calculation: 5 stages of inverters with W=5u, L=0.5u. The supply headroom is reduced by V_C. Delay per stage is approx C_load * V_swing / I_drive. Expected period is around 10-20ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The 0.5um channel length is relatively large for SKY130, which will limit the maximum frequency, aligning well with the paper's 80 MHz target.

tuning_range.description: The difference between the maximum and minimum oscillation frequencies over the control voltage range (0.6V to 1.2V).

sky130_expected.calculation: Frequency at VEA=0.6V minus Frequency at VEA=1.2V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The V-to-I converter changes V_C by a few hundred millivolts over the VEA range, modulating the frequency significantly.

kvco.description: VCO gain, representing the change in frequency per unit change in control voltage.

sky130_expected.reasoning: An increase in VEA increases V_C, which reduces the voltage headroom for the ring oscillator, resulting in a negative Kvco.

power_consumption.description: Average power consumption of the VCO at the nominal center frequency.

sky130_expected.calculation: Average current from VDD * 1.8V during steady-state oscillation.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The VCO alone consumes a small fraction of the total 125 mW reported for the entire digital controller chip.

step3_testbench.description: Measures the center frequency, tuning range, Kvco, and power consumption of the VCO by sweeping the control voltage (VEA) across three points (0.6V, 0.9V, 1.2V) using transient analysis.

XM1 N0 N3 N5 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N1 N0 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N8 N12 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}

XM5 N11 N4 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 N2 VBIAS VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}
XM7 N6 N6 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm7} w={W_xm7}
XM8 N1 VEA N5 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm8} w={W_xm8}

XM_T N6 N2 N3 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm_t} w={W_xm_t}
XM11 N4 N10 V_C GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm11} w={W_xm11}
XM_1 V_C V_C GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm_1} w={W_xm_1}
XM13 V_C N6 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm13} w={W_xm13}
XM14 N11 N4 V_C GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm14} w={W_xm14}
XM15 N10 N8 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm15} w={W_xm15}
XM16 N4 N10 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm16} w={W_xm16}

XM18 N10 N8 V_C GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm18} w={W_xm18}
XM19 N8 N12 V_C GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm19} w={W_xm19}
XM20 N12 N11 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm20} w={W_xm20}
XM21 N12 N11 V_C GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm21} w={W_xm21}

* DC Sources
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVBIAS VBIAS 0 0.99
VVEA VEA 0 0.9

* Missing load resistor for the source follower (XM_T) to establish V-to-I conversion
R_N3 N3 0 10k

* Behavioral source to create a robust zero-crossing signal for frequency measurement
B1 n_zero 0 V=V(n10)-0.5*V(V_C)-0.9

* Initial conditions to kickstart the ring oscillator
.ic v(n10)=0 v(n8)=1.8 v(n12)=0 v(n11)=1.8 v(n4)=0

.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.control
  * 1. Center Frequency and Power (VEA = 0.9V)
  tran 100p 500n
  meas tran t_period trig v(n_zero) val=0 rise=3 targ v(n_zero) val=0 rise=4
  let freq_mid = 1 / t_period
  print freq_mid
  
  let pwr = -i(VVDD)*1.8
  meas tran power_avg avg pwr from=100n to=500n
  print power_avg

  * 2. Low VEA (VEA = 0.6V) -> Higher Frequency
  alter VVEA 0.6
  tran 100p 500n
  meas tran t_period_low trig v(n_zero) val=0 rise=3 targ v(n_zero) val=0 rise=4
  let freq_high = 1 / t_period_low
  print freq_high

  * 3. High VEA (VEA = 1.2V) -> Lower Frequency
  alter VVEA 1.2
  tran 100p 500n
  meas tran t_period_high trig v(n_zero) val=0 rise=3 targ v(n_zero) val=0 rise=4
  let freq_low = 1 / t_period_high
  print freq_low

  * Calculate Kvco and Tuning Range
  let kvco = (freq_low - freq_high) / (1.2 - 0.6)
  print kvco
  
  let tuning_range = freq_high - freq_low
  print tuning_range
  
  quit
.endc
